status.en: 15 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 150% more than the week before, most of them in Kivu, Kinshasa and Kigali.
status.nb: 15 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 150 prosent flere enn uken før, flest i Kivu, Kinshasa og Kigali.

summary.en: M23 rebels have seized a major town in eastern DRC, breaking a ceasefire and intensifying clashes with the Congolese army. ADF gunmen continue killing civilians in Ituri province while an ISIL affiliate sustains itself through conflict gold. A drone strike hit Bunyakiri hospital, forcing MSF to move 76 patients, and a Chinese national was abducted with two people killed in an ambush at Kalemie. The conflict caused 1,158 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: M23‑opprørerne har tatt kontroll over en stor by i østlige DRC, brutt en våpenhvile og skjerpet kampene med den kongoske hæren. ADF-våpnere fortsetter å drepe sivile i Ituri-provinsen mens en IS-tilknyttet gruppe lever av gull fra konflikten. Et droneram rammet Bunyakiri-sykehuset, og MSF måtte flytte 76 pasienter, og en kinesisk nasjonal ble bortført mens to personer ble drept i et bakholdsangrep i Kalemie. Konflikten forårsaket 1 158 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: M23 campaign (2022–present)
background.extract: The M23 campaign is an ongoing series of military offensives launched by the March 23 Movement (M23), a Rwandan-backed rebel paramilitary group in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, since March 2022. In November 2021, M23 first launched attacks against the Congolese military (FARDC) and MONUSCO, seizing military positions in Ndiza, Cyanzu, and Runyoni in North Kivu Province. This coincided with the deployment of Uganda People's Defence Force (UPDF) to the region to combat the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), a Ugandan rebel group operating in the Congo's North Kivu and Ituri provinces.
